title: Chapter 16 — Anseriformes
description: Aquatic birds characterised by webbed feet, broad flat bills, and dense waterproofed plumage. The order includes ducks, geese, and swans, along with the more primitive screamers of South America. Many species undertake long seasonal migrations.

children.name: Aix
children.description: A genus of 2 ornate perching ducks — the Mandarin Duck of East Asia and the Wood Duck of North America — noted for their spectacular iridescent plumage and habit of nesting in tree cavities.

children.name: Aix galericulata
children.description: The mandarin duck is a perching duck species native to East and Northeast Asia. It is sexually dimorphic; the males are elaborately coloured, while the females have more subdued colours. It is a medium-sized duck, at 41–49 cm (16–19 in) long with a 65–75 cm (26–30 in) wingspan.

children.name: Aix sponsa
children.description: The wood duck or Carolina duck is a partially migratory species of perching duck found in North America. The male is one of the most colorful North American waterfowls.

children.name: Alopochen
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Egyptian Goose, a large, boldly patterned sheldgoose native to Africa south of the Sahara and the Nile Valley, now widely introduced in Europe.

children.name: Alopochen aegyptiaca
children.description: The Egyptian goose (Alopochen aegyptiaca) is an African member of the Anatidae family including ducks, geese, and swans.

children.name: Amazonetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Brazilian Teal, a small, chestnut-and-grey dabbling duck endemic to freshwater wetlands and gallery forests of South America.

children.name: Amazonetta brasiliensis
children.description: thumb| Amazonetta brasiliensis - [[MHNT]].

children.name: Anas
children.description: The largest genus of dabbling ducks with about 30 species, including the cosmopolitan Mallard, distributed across every continent; members feed by tipping head-down in shallow water rather than diving.

children.name: Anas acuta
children.description: The pintail or northern pintail is a duck species with wide geographic distribution that breeds in the northern areas of Europe and across the Palearctic and North America. It is migratory and winters south of its breeding range as far as the equator. Unusually for a bird with such a large range, it has no geographical subspecies, although the possibly conspecific duck Eaton's pintail is considered to be a separate species.

children.name: Anas albogularis
children.description: The Andaman teal (Anas albogularis) is a species of duck endemic to the Andaman archipelago in the Bay of Bengal.

children.name: Anas andium
children.description: The Andean teal (Anas andium) is a South American species of duck.

children.name: Anas aucklandica
children.description: The Auckland teal (Anas aucklandica) (), also known as Auckland Islands teal, is a species of dabbling duck of the genus Anas that is endemic to Auckland Islands south of New Zealand.

children.name: Anas capensis
children.description: The Cape teal (Anas capensis) also Cape wigeon or Cape widgeon is a 44–46 cm long dabbling duck of open wetlands in sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Anas castanea
children.description: The chestnut teal (Anas castanea) is a dabbling duck found in Australia.

children.name: Anas crecca
children.description: The Eurasian teal, common teal, or Eurasian green-winged teal is a common and widespread duck that breeds in temperate Eurosiberia and migrates south in winter. The Eurasian teal is often called simply the teal due to being the only one of these small dabbling ducks in much of its range. The bird gives its name to the blue-green colour teal.

children.name: Anas diazi
children.description: The Mexican duck (Anas diazi) is a species of dabbling duck that breeds in Mexico and the southwestern United States.

children.name: Anas drygalskii
children.description: A small, near-flightless teal endemic to the Crozet Islands in the southern Indian Ocean, split from the Kerguelen Teal on the basis of morphological and genetic differences. Like its Kerguelen relative it has reduced wing musculature and very limited flight capability — a consequence of evolving on islands without mammalian predators. Feeds on aquatic invertebrates in sheltered bogs, streams and coastal pools on the remote subantarctic archipelago. Named after Erich von Drygalski, the German geographer and polar explorer. IUCN Near Threatened.

children.name: Anas flavirostris
children.description: The yellow-billed teal is a South American species of duck. Like other teals, it belongs to the diverse genus Anas; more precisely it is one of the "true" teals of subgenus Nettion. It occurs in Argentina, the Falkland Islands, Chile, Peru, Bolivia, Uruguay, and Brazil.

children.name: Anas fulvigula
children.description: The mottled duck (Anas fulvigula) or mottled mallard is a medium-sized species of dabbling duck.

children.name: Anas gibberifrons
children.description: The Sunda teal (Anas gibberifrons), also known as the Bebek cokelat or Itik benjut, is a dabbling duck found in open wetlands in Indonesia and Timor-Leste.

children.name: Anas gracilis
children.description: The grey teal (Anas gracilis) is a dabbling duck found in open wetlands in Australia and New Zealand.

children.name: Anas laysanensis
children.description: The Laysan duck (Anas laysanensis), also known as the Laysan teal, and sometimes known by its Hawaiian name, koloa pōhaka, is a dabbling duck endemic to the Hawaiian Islands.

children.name: Anas luzonica
children.description: thumb|Philippine ducks in the [[Candaba Swamp]] The Philippine duck (Anas luzonica) is a large dabbling duck of the genus Anas.

children.name: Anas nesiotis
children.description: The Campbell teal or Campbell Island teal (Anas nesiotis) is a small, flightless, nocturnal species of dabbling duck of the genus Anas endemic to the Campbell Island group of New Zealand.

children.name: Anas platyrhynchos
children.description: The mallard or wild duck is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa. It has been introduced to New Zealand, Australia, Peru, Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, the Falkland Islands, and South Africa. Belonging to the subfamily Anatinae of the waterfowl family Anatidae, mallards live in wetlands, eat water plants and small animals, and are social animals preferring to congregate in groups or flocks of varying sizes.

children.name: Anas platyrhynchos domesticus
children.description: Anas platyrhynchos domesticus (Domestic Duck) is a domesticated waterfowl species found worldwide.

children.name: Anas poecilorhyncha
children.description: The Indian spot-billed duck (Anas poecilorhyncha) is a species of large dabbling duck that is a non-migratory breeding duck throughout freshwater wetlands in the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Anas haringtoni
children.description: A large dabbling duck of mainland Southeast Asia, recently elevated from a subspecies of the Indian Spot-billed Duck on the basis of genetic and morphological differences. Its range extends from Myanmar and southern China through Indochina to the Malay Peninsula. Distinguished from the Indian nominate by subtler plumage differences, particularly in the facial pattern and speculum markings. Found on rivers, lakes, and paddy fields throughout the lowlands of mainland Southeast Asia. Named after Harington, the British officer who collected specimens in Burma in the early 20th century.

children.name: Anas rubripes
children.description: The American black duck is a large dabbling duck in the family Anatidae. It was described by William Brewster in 1902. It is the heaviest species in the genus Anas, weighing 720–1,640 g (1.6–3.6 lb) on average and measuring 54–59 cm (21–23 in) in length with an 88–95 cm (35–37 in) wingspan.

children.name: Anas sparsa
children.description: The African black duck (Anas sparsa) is a species of duck of the genus Anas.

children.name: Anas leucostigma
children.description: A dark, river-dwelling duck of the East African highlands and Rift Valley, elevated from a subspecies of the African Black Duck on the basis of its disjunct range and morphological distinctiveness. Found from Ethiopia and Sudan south through Kenya and Uganda to Tanzania, inhabiting fast-flowing rivers and streams in montane and highland zones. Like its southern relative it favours clear, rocky watercourses over still water. The name leucostigma ('white-marked') refers to the white speckling on the dark plumage. Its isolation in East African highland river systems has led to consistent differences in plumage and size that support species-level recognition.

children.name: Anas superciliosa
children.description: The Pacific black duck (Anas superciliosa), commonly known as the PBD, is a dabbling duck found in much of Indonesia, New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and many islands in the southwestern Pacific, reaching to the Caroline Islands in the north and French Polynesia in the east.

children.name: Anas wyvilliana
children.description: The Hawaiian duck (Anas wyvilliana) or koloa is a species of bird in the family Anatidae that is endemic to the large islands of Hawai i.

children.name: Anas oustaleti
children.description: The Mariana mallard or Oustalet's duck (Anas oustaleti) is an extinct species of duck of the genus Anas that was endemic to the Mariana Islands.

children.name: Anser
children.description: A genus of 11 grey geese — including the Greylag, Bean, Snow, and Bar-headed Goose — breeding across the Holarctic and notable for long-distance migrations between Arctic breeding grounds and temperate wintering areas.

children.name: Anser albifrons
children.description: The greater white-fronted goose is a species of goose, closely related to the smaller lesser white-fronted goose. The greater white-fronted goose is migratory, breeding in northern Canada, Alaska, Greenland, and Russia, and winters farther south in North America, Europe, and Asia. It is named for the patch of white feathers bordering the base of its bill; its specific name albifrons comes from the Latin albus "white" and frons "forehead".

children.name: Anser anser
children.description: The greylag goose (Anser anser) is a species of large goose in the waterfowl family Anatidae and the type species of the genus Anser.

children.name: Anser anser domesticus
children.description: Anser anser domesticus (Domestic Goose) is a domesticated waterfowl species found worldwide.

children.name: Anser brachyrhynchus
children.description: The pink-footed goose is a goose which breeds in eastern Greenland, Iceland, Svalbard, and recently Novaya Zemlya. It is migratory, wintering in northwest Europe, especially Ireland, Great Britain, the Netherlands, and western Denmark. The name is often abbreviated in colloquial usage to "pinkfoot".

children.name: Anser caerulescens
children.description: The snow goose is a species of goose native to North America. Both white and dark morphs exist, the latter often known as blue goose. Its name derives from the typically white plumage.

children.name: Anser canagicus
children.description: The emperor goose (Anser canagicus), also known as the beach goose or the painted goose, is a waterfowl species in the family Anatidae, which contains the ducks, geese, and swans.

children.name: Anser cygnoides
children.description: The swan goose (Anser cygnoides) is a large goose with a natural breeding range in inland Mongolia, Northeast China, and the Russian Far East.

children.name: Anser erythropus
children.description: The lesser white-fronted goose (Anser erythropus) is a goose closely related to the larger greater white-fronted goose (A.

children.name: Anser fabalis
children.description: The taiga bean goose is a species of goose that breeds in northern Europe and Asia. It is migratory and winters further south in Europe and Asia. This and the tundra bean goose were recognised as separate species by the International Ornithologists' Union and the American Ornithological Society from 2007, but are still considered a single species by some other authorities, notably BirdLife International and the IUCN.

children.name: Anser rossii
children.description: Ross's goose is a white goose with black wingtips and a relatively short neck. It is the smallest of the three white geese that breed in North America. It is similar in appearance to a white-phase snow goose, but about 40% smaller.

children.name: Anser serrirostris
children.description: The tundra bean goose is a goose that breeds in northern Siberia. This and the taiga bean goose are recognised as separate species by the American Ornithological Society and International Ornithologists' Union, but are considered a single species by other authorities. It is migratory and winters further south in Asia.

children.name: Asarcornis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the endangered White-winged Duck, a large, dark perching duck with white wing patches restricted to lowland forest rivers and wetlands of South and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Aythya
children.description: A genus of 12 diving ducks — including pochards, scaups, and the Canvasback — found across the Northern Hemisphere, characterised by their compact bodies and ability to dive deeply for aquatic plants and invertebrates.

children.name: Aythya affinis
children.description: The lesser scaup (Aythya affinis) is a small North American diving duck that migrates south as far as Central America in winter.

children.name: Aythya ferina
children.description: The common pochard, known simply as pochard in the United Kingdom, is a medium-sized diving duck in the family Anatidae. It is widespread across the Palearctic. It breeds primarily in Scandinavia and the steppe regions of Siberia, and winters farther south and west.

children.name: Aythya fuligula
children.description: The tufted duck is a small diving duck with a population of nearly one million birds, found in northern Eurasia. They are partially migratory. The scientific name is derived from Ancient Greek aithuia, an unidentified seabird mentioned by authors such as Hesychius and Aristotle, and Latin fuligo 'soot' and gula 'throat'.

children.name: Aythya innotata
children.description: The Madagascar pochard or Madagascan pochard (Aythya innotata; ) is an extremely rare diving duck of the genus Aythya.

children.name: Aythya marila
children.description: The greater scaup, just scaup in Europe or, colloquially, "bluebill" in North America, is a mid-sized diving duck, larger than the closely related lesser scaup and tufted duck. It spends the summer months breeding in Iceland, east across Scandinavia, northern Russia and Siberia, Alaska, and northern Canada. During the winter, it migrates south to the coasts of Europe, eastern Asia, and North America.

children.name: Aythya nyroca
children.description: The ferruginous duck (Aythya nyroca), also known as the ferruginous pochard, common white-eye or white-eyed pochard, is a medium-sized diving duck native to the Palearctic.

children.name: Biziura
children.description: A monotypic Australian genus containing the Musk Duck, a large stiff-tailed diving duck remarkable for the leathery lobe hanging beneath the male's bill and its distinctive musky odour.

children.name: Biziura lobata
children.description: The musk duck (Biziura lobata) is a highly aquatic, stiff-tailed duck native to southern Australia.

children.name: Branta
children.description: A genus of 6 black geese — including the Canada Goose, Barnacle Goose, and Brent Goose — distinguished from grey Anser geese by their dark plumage with contrasting white face or neck patches, breeding in Arctic and subarctic regions worldwide.

children.name: Branta bernicla
children.description: The brant or brent goose is a small goose in the genus Branta. There are three subspecies, all of which winter along temperate-zone sea-coasts and breed on the high-Arctic tundra.

children.name: Branta canadensis
children.description: The Canada goose is a large species of goose with a black head and neck, white cheeks, white under its chin, and a brown body. It is native to the Arctic and temperate regions of North America, and it is occasionally found during migration across the Atlantic in northern Europe. It has been introduced to France, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Scandinavia, New Zealand, Japan, Chile, Argentina, and the Falkland Islands.

children.name: Branta hutchinsii
children.description: The cackling goose (Branta hutchinsii) is a species of goose found in North America and East Asia.

children.name: Branta leucopsis
children.description: The barnacle goose is a species of goose that belongs to the genus Branta of black geese, which contains species with extensive black in the plumage, distinguishing them from the grey Anser species. Despite its superficial similarity to the brant goose, genetic analysis has shown its closest relative is the cackling goose.

children.name: Bucephala
children.description: A genus of 3 goldeneye and bufflehead diving ducks of the Northern Hemisphere, characterised by large rounded heads, rapid wingbeats producing a whistling sound in flight, and nest cavities in trees near boreal lakes.

children.name: Bucephala albeola
children.description: The bufflehead is a small sea duck of the genus Bucephala, the goldeneyes. It breeds in Alaska and Canada and migrates in winter to southern North America. This species was first described by Carl Linnaeus in his landmark 1758 10th edition of Systema Naturae as Anas albeola.

children.name: Bucephala clangula
children.description: The common goldeneye or simply goldeneye is a medium-sized sea duck of the genus Bucephala, the goldeneyes. Its closest relative is the similar Barrow's goldeneye. The genus name is derived from the Ancient Greek boukephalos, a reference to the bulbous head shape of the bufflehead.

children.name: Cairina
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Muscovy Duck, a large, iridescent black-and-white perching duck native to Central and South America that is widely domesticated worldwide for meat production.

children.name: Cairina moschata
children.description: The Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) is a species of duck native to the Americas, from the Lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas and Mexico south to Argentina and Uruguay.

children.name: Camptorhynchus
children.description: An extinct monotypic genus containing the Labrador Duck, a sea duck that inhabited the Atlantic coast of North America and became the first North American bird species confirmed extinct in the modern era.

children.name: Camptorhynchus labradorius
children.description: The Labrador duck (Camptorhynchus labradorius) is an extinct North American duck species.

children.name: Callonetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Ringed Teal, a small, colourful dabbling duck of subtropical South American forests and wetlands, unusual among ducks in that the male assists with chick-rearing.

children.name: Callonetta leucophrys
children.description: The ringed teal (Callonetta leucophrys) is a small duck of marshes, pools, and forest wetlands native to south-central South America.

children.name: Cereopsis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Cape Barren Goose, a large, pale grey goose with a distinctive yellow-green cere found on islands off southern Australia, unusual for a waterfowl in its preference for grazing on dry land.

children.name: Chenonetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Australian Wood Duck, a goose-like dabbling duck widespread across grasslands and lightly wooded areas of Australia, often seen grazing far from water.

children.name: Chenonetta jubata
children.description: The Australian wood duck, maned duck or maned goose (Chenonetta jubata) is a dabbling duck found throughout much of Australia.

children.name: Chloephaga
children.description: A genus of 5 South American sheldgeese — including the Kelp Goose and Upland Goose — mostly found in Patagonia and the Falkland Islands, where they graze on grasslands and coastal meadows.

children.name: Chloephaga hybrida
children.description: The kelp goose (Chloephaga hybrida) is a species of waterfowl in tribe the Tadornini of the subfamily Anserinae.

children.name: Chloephaga melanoptera
children.description: The Andean goose (Chloephaga melanoptera) is a species of waterfowl in tribe Tadornini of subfamily Anserinae.

children.name: Chloephaga picta
children.description: | image_caption = Male, Argentina | image2 = | image2_caption = Female, Chile both C.

children.name: Clangula
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Long-tailed Duck, an Arctic sea duck recognisable by the male's long tail streamers and complex seasonal plumage, which dives to extraordinary depths of up to 60 m to feed.

children.name: Clangula hyemalis
children.description: The long-tailed duck is a medium-sized sea duck that breeds in the tundra and taiga regions of the arctic and winters along the northern coastlines of the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. It is the only member of the genus Clangula.

children.name: Coscoroba
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Coscoroba Swan, the smallest swan, entirely white with red bill and feet, found in southern South America from central Chile and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego.

children.name: Coscoroba coscoroba
children.description: The coscoroba swan (Coscoroba coscoroba) is a species of waterfowl in the subfamily Anserinae of the family Anatidae.

children.name: Cyanochen
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Blue-winged Goose, a small, brown Afrotropical sheldgoose endemic to the Ethiopian Highlands, where it grazes on montane grasslands at high altitudes.

children.name: Cygnus
children.description: A genus of 6 swans — the largest waterfowl — including the Mute, Whooper, Trumpeter, and Black Swan, found on every continent except Antarctica, characterised by long necks, powerful wingbeats, and lifelong pair bonds.

children.name: Cygnus atratus
children.description: The black swan (Cygnus atratus) is a large waterbird, a species of swan which breeds mainly in the southeast and southwest regions of Australia.

children.name: Cygnus buccinator
children.description: The trumpeter swan (Cygnus buccinator), or simply the trumpeter, is a species of swan found in North America.

children.name: Cygnus columbianus
children.description: The tundra swan is a Holarctic species of swan and the smallest of the Holarctic swans. It comprises two subspecies, which are sometimes treated as separate species: Bewick's swan of the Palaearctic and the whistling swan of the Nearctic.

children.name: Cygnus bewickii
children.description: The tundra swan (Cygnus columbianus) is a species of swan of the Holarctic.

children.name: Cygnus cygnus
children.description: The whooper swan, also known as the common swan, is a large northern hemisphere swan. It is the Eurasian counterpart of the North American trumpeter swan.

children.name: Cygnus olor
children.description: The mute swan is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order. It is native to much of Europe and parts of Asia and the far north of Africa. It is an introduced species in North America, home to the largest populations outside of its native range, with additional smaller introductions in Australasia and Southern Africa.

children.name: Dendrocygna
children.description: A genus of 8 whistling-ducks with a pantropical distribution across the Americas, Africa, and Asia-Pacific, distinguished by their upright stance, long necks and legs, and loud whistling calls given in flight.

children.name: Dendrocygna arcuata
children.description: The wandering whistling duck (Dendrocygna arcuata) is a species of whistling duck.

children.name: Dendrocygna bicolor
children.description: The fulvous whistling duck or fulvous tree duck (Dendrocygna bicolor) is a species of whistling duck that breeds across the world's tropical regions in much of Mexico and South America, the West Indies, the southern United States, sub-Saharan Africa and the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Dendrocygna eytoni
children.description: The plumed whistling duck (Dendrocygna eytoni), also called the grass whistling duck, is a species of bird in the whistling duck subfamily of the family Anatidae.

children.name: Dendrocygna guttata
children.description: The spotted whistling duck (Dendrocygna guttata) is a member of the duck family Anatidae.

children.name: Dendrocygna javanica
children.description: The lesser whistling duck (Dendrocygna javanica), also known as Indian whistling duck or lesser whistling teal, is a species of whistling duck that breeds in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Heteronetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Black-headed Duck of southern South America, the only obligate brood parasite in the duck family, laying its eggs exclusively in the nests of other waterbirds.

children.name: Histrionicus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Harlequin Duck, a small sea duck with boldly patterned blue, chestnut, and white plumage that breeds along fast-flowing mountain torrents in North America and Iceland, wintering on rocky coastlines.

children.name: Histrionicus histrionicus
children.description: The harlequin duck (Histrionicus histrionicus) is a small sea duck.

children.name: Hymenolaimus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Blue Duck, a torrent-specialist endemic to fast-flowing mountain streams of New Zealand, with streamlined body, pink fleshy bill lobes, and chestnut-spotted blue-grey plumage.

children.name: Hymenolaimus malacorhynchos
children.description: The blue duck (Hymenolaimus malacorhynchos) or whio is a member of the duck, goose and swan family Anatidae endemic to New Zealand.

children.name: Lophodytes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Hooded Merganser, a small North American fish-eating duck renowned for the male's large fan-shaped white crest edged in black, which nests in tree cavities near wooded lakes and ponds.

children.name: Lophodytes cucullatus
children.description: The hooded merganser (Lophodytes cucullatus) is a species of fish-eating duck in the subfamily Anatinae.

children.name: Lophonetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Crested Duck, a large, pale brownish dabbling duck with a small wispy crest found along coasts, rivers, and high-altitude lakes of Patagonia and the Andes.

children.name: Lophonetta specularioides
children.description: The crested duck or South American crested duck (Lophonetta specularioides) is a species of duck native to South America, belonging to the monotypic genus Lophonetta.

children.name: Malacorhynchus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Pink-eared Duck, a small Australian dabbling duck with a unique large spatula-shaped bill fringed with lamellae for filter-feeding, and a distinctive black-and-white barred pattern.

children.name: Mareca
children.description: A genus of 6 dabbling ducks (including 1 extinct species) known as wigeons and the Falcated Duck, found across the Holarctic and South America, characterised by rounded heads, short bills, and a preference for grazing on short grass and aquatic vegetation.

children.name: Mareca americana
children.description: The American wigeon, also known as the baldpate, is a species of dabbling duck found in North America. Formerly assigned to Anas, this species is classified with the other wigeons in the dabbling duck genus Mareca. It is the New World counterpart of the Eurasian wigeon.

children.name: Mareca falcata
children.description: The falcated duck or falcated teal (Mareca falcata) is a gadwall-sized dabbling duck from the east Palearctic (East Siberia and Mongolia to North Japan; wintering to India).

children.name: Mareca penelope
children.description: The Eurasian wigeon or European wigeon, also known as the widgeon or wigeon, is one of three extant species of wigeon in the dabbling duck genus Mareca. It is common and widespread within its Palearctic range.

children.name: Mareca strepera
children.description: The gadwall is a common and widespread dabbling duck in the family Anatidae.

children.name: Mareca couesi
children.description: An extinct island gadwall endemic to Fanning Atoll (now Tabuaeran) in the central Pacific Ocean, known from a small number of specimens collected by the USS Tanager expedition in the 1870s. Closely related to the Gadwall, it represented a distinct island form that succumbed to hunting pressure and predation by introduced animals. Named after American army surgeon and naturalist Elliott Coues.

children.name: Marmaronetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Marbled Duck, a pale mottled diving-dabbling duck of shallow, vegetated wetlands from the Mediterranean to Central Asia, considered vulnerable due to habitat loss.

children.name: Marmaronetta angustirostris
children.description: The marbled duck or marbled teal (Marmaronetta angustirostris) is a medium-sized species of duck from southern Europe, northern Africa, and western and central Asia.

children.name: Melanitta
children.description: A genus of 6 scoters — large, mostly black sea ducks of the Northern Hemisphere — that breed on Arctic and boreal lakes but winter in large flocks on coastal seas, diving for molluscs and crustaceans.

children.name: Melanitta americana
children.description: The black scoter or American scoter (Melanitta americana) is a large sea duck, in length.

children.name: Melanitta fusca
children.description: The velvet scoter is a large sea duck, which breeds over the far north of Europe and the Palearctic west of the Yenisey basin. The genus name is derived from Ancient Greek melas "black" and netta "duck". The species name is from the Latin fuscus "dusky brown".

children.name: Melanitta nigra
children.description: The common scoter is a large sea duck, 43–54 cm (17–21 in) in length, which breeds over the far north of Europe and the Palearctic east to the Olenyok River. The black scoter of North America and eastern Siberia was formerly considered to be a subspecies.

children.name: Melanitta perspicillata
children.description: The surf scoter (Melanitta perspicillata) is a large sea duck native to North America.

children.name: Merganetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Torrent Duck, a striking Andean specialist that forages in fast-flowing Andean rivers and streams from Venezuela to Tierra del Fuego, with a streamlined body and stiff tail for navigating white water.

children.name: Merganetta armata
children.description: The torrent duck (Merganetta armata) is a member of the duck, goose and swan family Anatidae.

children.name: Mergellus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Smew, a small Eurasian merganser in which the white-and-black male is among the most elegant of ducks, breeding in boreal forest lakes and wintering on European and Asian coasts.

children.name: Mergellus albellus
children.description: The smew is a species of duck and is the only living member of the genus Mergellus. The genus is closely related to Mergus and is sometimes included in it; genetic studies have shown that it is the sister taxon to Mergus and Lophodytes. The smew has hybridised with the common goldeneye.

children.name: Mergus
children.description: A genus of 5 mergansers (including 1 extinct species) — including the Common Merganser and Red-breasted Merganser — found across the Holarctic, characterised by serrated bills for gripping fish and a long, streamlined body for underwater pursuit.

children.name: Mergus merganser
children.description: The common merganser or goosander is a large sea duck of rivers and lakes in forested areas of Europe, Asia, and North America. The common merganser eats mainly fish. It nests in holes in trees.

children.name: Mergus serrator
children.description: The red-breasted merganser is a duck species that is native to much of the temperate to subarctic Northern Hemisphere. The red breast that gives the species its common name is only displayed by males in breeding plumage. Individuals fly rapidly, and feed by diving from the surface to pursue aquatic animals underwater, using serrated bills to capture slippery fish.

children.name: Neochen
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Orinoco Goose, a pale-bodied sheldgoose with chestnut flanks found along forested river banks and sandbars in the Amazon and Orinoco basins of South America.

children.name: Neochen jubata
children.description: The Orinoco goose (Neochen jubata) is a species of waterfowl in the tribe Tadornini of subfamily Anserinae.

children.name: Netta
children.description: A genus of 4 pochards — the Red-crested Pochard, Rosy-billed Pochard, Southern Pochard, and African Pochard — medium-sized diving ducks distributed across Europe, Africa, and South America, often found on large open lakes.

children.name: Netta brunnea
children.description: A medium-sized diving pochard of sub-Saharan African freshwater lakes and reservoirs, split from the South American Southern Pochard (N. erythrophthalma) on the basis of morphological and genetic differentiation. The male has a dark reddish-brown head, white flanks and a pale blue-grey bill; the female is browner overall. Found from Ethiopia and the Congo basin south to the Cape, favouring deep, open waters with fringing vegetation. Historically common but undergoing significant declines due to wetland drainage, hunting pressure, and capture for the live bird trade. IUCN Vulnerable.

children.name: Netta peposaca
children.description: The rosy-billed pochard, alternatively named rosybill or rosybill pochard, is a member of family Anatidae. Though classified as a diving duck, this pochard feeds more like a dabbling duck feeding on seeds roots, sedges, aquatic plants and other grasses. Netta is Ancient Greek for "duck" and peposaca is a transcription of the Guaraní name of this species which means "showy wings", referring to the broad white stripe that is only visible with stretched out wings.

children.name: Nettapus
children.description: A genus of 3 pygmy geese — the smallest waterfowl — found on tropical wetlands across sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Australasia, with short goose-like bills and a preference for floating vegetation.

children.name: Nettapus coromandelianus
children.description: The cotton pygmy goose or cotton teal (Nettapus coromandelianus) is a small perching duck which breeds in Asia, Southeast Asia extending south and east to Queensland where they are sometimes called white-quilled pygmy goose.

children.name: Nomonyx
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Masked Duck, a small, secretive stiff-tailed duck of tropical freshwater marshes from Mexico and the Caribbean through South America, closely related to Oxyura.

children.name: Nomonyx dominicus
children.description: The masked duck (Nomonyx dominicus) is a tiny stiff-tailed duck ranging through the tropical Americas.

children.name: Oxyura
children.description: A genus of 6 stiff-tailed ducks found on freshwater lakes in the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Australia, distinguished by their stiff fan-like tails held erect during courtship and compact diving bodies.

children.name: Oxyura ferruginea
children.description: The Andean duck (Oxyura ferruginea) is a bird species native to the Andean Mountains of South America, one of the stiff-tailed ducks.

children.name: Oxyura jamaicensis
children.description: The ruddy duck (Oxyura jamaicensis) is a species of duck, one of six extant species of stiff-tailed duck (genus Oxyura).

children.name: Oxyura maccoa
children.description: The Maccoa duck (Oxyura maccoa) is a stiff-tailed diving duck found across Eastern and Southern Africa.

children.name: Oxyura vittata
children.description: The lake duck (Oxyura vittata) is a small, South American stiff-tailed duck.

children.name: Plectropterus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Spur-winged Goose, Africa's largest waterfowl, a black-and-white sheldgoose with a prominent carpal spur on each wing, widespread in sub-Saharan African wetlands and grasslands.

children.name: Polysticta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Steller's Eider, the smallest of the four eider species, breeding on tundra wetlands of Alaska and Arctic Russia and wintering in dense flocks on shallow Alaskan and Scandinavian coasts.

children.name: Pteronetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Hartlaub's Duck, a dark chestnut-and-black perching duck of West and Central African tropical forest streams and rivers, named after German ornithologist Gustav Hartlaub.

children.name: Radjah
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Radjah Shelduck, a white-and-chestnut shelduck of mangroves, tidal flats, and coastal wetlands in New Guinea and northern Australia, also known as the Burdekin Duck.

children.name: Radjah radjah
children.description: The radjah shelduck (Radjah radjah) is a species of shelduck found mostly in New Guinea and Australia, and also on some of the Moluccas.

children.name: Rhodonessa
children.description: An extinct monotypic genus containing the Pink-headed Duck, a strikingly coloured diving duck of South Asian swamplands, last recorded in the wild in 1935 and now feared extinct.

children.name: Salvadorina
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Salvadori's Duck, a cryptically patterned torrent duck endemic to the swift mountain streams of New Guinea, considered a relict waterfowl with uncertain family placement.

children.name: Sarkidiornis
children.description: A genus of 2 comb ducks found in tropical wetlands of Africa, South Asia, and South America, recognised by the large black knob on top of the male's bill that enlarges during the breeding season.

children.name: Sarkidiornis sylvicola
children.description: | range_map = Sarkidiornis sylvicola map.svg.

children.name: Sibirionetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Baikal Teal, a striking East Asian dabbling duck with an ornate green, yellow, and black face pattern in the male, breeding in Siberian boreal forests and migrating to East Asia.

children.name: Sibirionetta formosa
children.description: The Baikal teal (Sibirionetta formosa), also called the bimaculate duck or squawk duck, is a dabbling duck that breeds in eastern Russia and winters in East Asia.

children.name: Somateria
children.description: A genus of 3 large eider sea ducks of Arctic and subarctic coasts — Common, Spectacled, and King Eider — famous for the female's down used to line nests, which is harvested commercially as eiderdown.

children.name: Somateria fischeri
children.description: The spectacled eider (pronounced ) (Somateria fischeri) is a large sea duck that breeds on the coasts of Alaska and northeastern Siberia.

children.name: Somateria mollissima
children.description: The common eider, also called St. Cuthbert's duck or Cuddy's duck, is a large sea-duck that is distributed over the northern coasts of Europe, North America and eastern Siberia. It breeds in Arctic and some northern temperate regions, but winters somewhat farther south in temperate zones, when it can form large flocks on coastal waters.

children.name: Somateria spectabilis
children.description: The king eider is a large sea duck that breeds along Northern Hemisphere Arctic coasts of northeast Europe, North America and Asia. The birds spend most of the year in coastal marine ecosystems at high latitudes, and migrate to Arctic tundra to breed in June and July. They lay four to seven eggs in a scrape on the ground lined with grass and down.

children.name: Spatula
children.description: A genus of 10 shovelers and teals with a near-cosmopolitan distribution, characterised by broad, spatula-shaped bills with dense lamellae that enable efficient filter-feeding on plankton and invertebrates in shallow water.

children.name: Spatula cyanoptera
children.description: The cinnamon teal is a species of duck found in western North and South America. It is a small dabbling duck, with bright reddish plumage on the male and duller brown plumage on the female. It lives in marshes and ponds, and feeds mostly on plants.

children.name: Spatula discors
children.description: The blue-winged teal is a species of bird in the duck, goose, and swan family Anatidae. One of the smaller members of the dabbling duck group, it occurs in North America, where it breeds from southern Alaska to Nova Scotia, and south to northern Texas. It winters along the Pacific and Atlantic coasts and south into the Caribbean islands and Central America.

children.name: Spatula puna
children.description: The Puna teal is a species of dabbling duck in the family Anatidae. It was at one time regarded as a subspecies of the silver teal .

children.name: Spatula querquedula
children.description: The garganey is a small dabbling duck. It breeds in much of Europe and across the Palearctic, but is strictly migratory, with the entire population moving to Africa, India, Bangladesh and Australasia during the winter of the Northern hemisphere, where large flocks can occur. This species was first described by Carl Linnaeus in his landmark 1758 10th edition of Systema Naturae.

children.name: Spatula rhynchotis
children.description: The Australasian shoveler (Spatula rhynchotis) is a species of dabbling duck in the genus Spatula.

children.name: Spatula smithii
children.description: The Cape shoveler or Cape shoveller (Spatula smithii) is a species of dabbling duck of the genus Spatula.

children.name: Spatula versicolor
children.description: The silver teal or versicolor teal is a species of dabbling duck in the genus Spatula. It breeds in South America.

children.name: Speculanas
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Bronze-winged Duck, a dark, chocolate-brown dabbling duck with a green wing speculum found along fast-flowing Andean and Patagonian rivers and lakes.

children.name: Stictonetta
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Freckled Duck, a cryptically speckled Australian waterfowl considered one of the most primitive living ducks, occurring in shallow freshwater swamps and lakes of southern Australia.

children.name: Stictonetta naevosa
children.description: The freckled duck (Stictonetta naevosa) is a waterfowl species endemic to Australia.

children.name: Tachyeres
children.description: A genus of 4 steamer-ducks restricted to the coasts and cold lakes of southern South America and the Falkland Islands, three species of which are flightless; they use their wings as paddles to propel themselves across water.

children.name: Tachyeres brachypterus
children.description: The Falkland steamer duck (Tachyeres brachypterus) is a species of flightless duck found on the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Tachyeres patachonicus
children.description: The flying steamer duck (Tachyeres patachonicus), also known as the flying steamer-duck or flying steamerduck, is a species of South American duck in the family Anatidae.

children.name: Tachyeres pteneres
children.description: The flightless steamer-duck (Tachyeres pteneres), Magellanic flightless steamer-duck, or Fuegian steamer duck, is a flightless duck native to South America.

children.name: Tadorna
children.description: A genus of 6 shelducks — large, goose-like ducks with striking patterned plumage — found from Western Europe to East Asia and Australia, often nesting in burrows and grazing on invertebrates along coasts and estuaries.

children.name: Tadorna cristata
children.description: The crested shelduck (Tadorna cristata) or Korean crested shelduck is a species of bird in the family Anatidae.

children.name: Tadorna ferruginea
children.description: The ruddy shelduck is a bird species in the family Anatidae. It is a distinctive waterfowl, 58 to 70 cm in length with a wingspan of 110 to 135 cm. It has orange-brown body plumage with a paler head, while the tail and the flight feathers in the wings are black, contrasting with the white wing-coverts.

children.name: Tadorna tadorna
children.description: The common shelduck is a waterfowl species of the shelduck genus Tadorna. It is widespread and common in the Palearctic, in Europe and northwest Africa mainly breeding on temperate coasts, saline pools and estuaries, and in Asia on inland salt lakes; increasingly it is also using open freshwater habitats inland. Wintering is in temperate to subtropical regions.

children.name: Tadorna tadornoides
children.description: The Australian shelduck (Tadorna tadornoides), also known as the chestnut-breasted shelduck or mountain duck, is a shelduck, a group of large goose-like ducks part of the bird family Anatidae.

children.name: Tadorna variegata
children.description: The paradise shelduck (Tadorna variegata), also known as the paradise duck, or in Māori, is a species of shelduck, a group of goose-like ducks, which is endemic to New Zealand.

children.name: Thalassornis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the White-backed Duck, a small diving duck of sub-Saharan African and Madagascar freshwater lakes with dense aquatic vegetation, anatomically intermediate between stiff-tailed ducks and whistling-ducks.

children.name: Anhima
children.description: A monotypic genus distinguished by a long, thin horn-like spike projecting forward from the forehead. These large, bulky waterfowl inhabit tropical wetlands of South America.

children.name: Anhima cornuta
children.description: The horned screamer (Anhima cornuta) is a species of bird that belongs to a relatively small family, the Anhimidae, which occurs in wetlands of tropical South America.

children.name: Chauna
children.description: Geese-like screamers with a short crest and a prominent spur on the leading edge of each wing used in combat. They are highly territorial and mate for life.

children.name: Chauna chavaria
children.description: The northern screamer (Chauna chavaria) is a species of bird in family Anhimidae of the waterfowl order Anseriformes.

children.name: Chauna torquata
children.description: The southern screamer (Chauna torquata) is a species of bird in family Anhimidae of the waterfowl order Anseriformes.

children.name: Anseranas
children.description: A monotypic genus representing an ancient lineage of waterfowl with a partially fused webbing and a distinctive knob on the crown. It is the sole surviving member of its family and retains several primitive anatomical features.

children.name: Anseranas semipalmata
children.description: The magpie goose (Anseranas semipalmata) is the sole living representative species of the family Anseranatidae.
